12: 
13: > Language convention (binding for this report, spec S1): every number below is either **SOURCE-BACKED**
14: > (imported from frozen Phase-4 production data, workspace-verified drawings/reports, or confirmed ratings),
15: > **DERIVED** (computed from SOURCE-BACKED inputs by shipped MATLAB code), **USER_ASSERTED_PENDING_DOC**
16: > (user-supplied 7UM622 values listed in spec S3, numerically separated, status PENDING-DOC-INGEST),

20: > simulated. Coordination shortfalls are "study-setting coordination shortfalls," never verdicts about installed
21: > equipment. TCCs are split into PHYSICAL/SOURCE-BACKED vs GENERIC STUDY classes. All relay data are **study

25: ---
26: 
27: ## 1. Executive summary
28: 
29: Phase-5b applies a physical protection architecture plus a qualified backup-OC/EF coordination study to the
30: frozen Phase-4 production fault package for Ashuganj South, covering 2 cases (`LF360_GAT_OUT`,
31: `LF360_GAT_IN`) x 5 fault locations (F1–F5) x 4 fault types (LLL/LG/LL/LLG) = 40 backbone rows.
32: 
33: Headline v2 results (each reproduced from the shipped `results/phase5_protection_v2/` CSVs, read with
34: `readtable(fp, 'Delimiter', ',')`):
35: 
36: - Study pickups (v2, as found): GEN-51-SI **17170.8 A** primary (1.20xImax 14309 A), GEN-51N-SI-STUDY **5 A**
37:   primary (SENSITIVE retained case), GSUT-HV-51 **1380 A** primary via 1600/1, GIS-Q0-51 **1043.94798235109 A**
38:   primary via 1600/1 (`phase5_relay_settings.csv`, 8 rows). Separate PHYSICAL baseline GEN-51-SIEMENS-BL
39:   **17171 A** primary (1.1447 A secondary via 15000/1, DT-??, tdef 3.00 s ?? PENDING-COORDINATION,
40:   USER_ASSERTED_PENDING_DOC, inverse prohibited — never dispatched to `phase5_time`).
41: - Coordination matrix v2 (96 rows, as found): **FAIL = 20, NO-TRIP = 28, NO-PAIR = 24,
42:   NOT DETERMINABLE FROM AVAILABLE DATA = 24, PASS = 0 (production-v2, 96 rows)**. Identical counts appear in
43:   `phase5_coordination_margins.csv`. No margin was tuned; shortfalls are study-setting coordination shortfalls
44:   reported honestly (see Sections 9 and 17).
45: - Breaker duty v2 (81 rows, as found): **40 x Q0 NOT DETERMINABLE FROM AVAILABLE DATA + 40 x 52G PASS +
46:   1 x Q0 NOTE**. That is 40 Q0 rows with no interrupting rating sourced, 40 52G rows PASS vs the sourced

> equipment. TCCs are split into PHYSICAL/SOURCE-BACKED vs GENERIC STUDY classes. All relay data are **study
> settings** evaluated in a **qualified model**. The peak current `ip` is a borrowed-shape design-defined quantity
> (informational only, never a breaker-duty input).

---

## 1. Executive summary

Phase-5b applies a physical protection architecture plus a qualified backup-OC/EF coordination study to the
frozen Phase-4 production fault package for Ashuganj South, covering 2 cases (`LF360_GAT_OUT`,
`LF360_GAT_IN`) x 5 fault locations (F1–F5) x 4 fault types (LLL/LG/LL/LLG) = 40 backbone rows.

Headline v2 results (each reproduced from the shipped `results/phase5_protection_v2/` CSVs, read with
`readtable(fp, 'Delimiter', ',')`):

- Study pickups (v2, as found): GEN-51-SI **17170.8 A** primary (1.20xImax 14309 A), GEN-51N-SI-STUDY **5 A**
  primary (SENSITIVE retained case), GSUT-HV-51 **1380 A** primary via 1600/1, GIS-Q0-51 **1043.94798235109 A**
  primary via 1600/1 (`phase5_relay_settings.csv`, 8 rows). Separate PHYSICAL baseline GEN-51-SIEMENS-BL
  **17171 A** primary (1.1447 A secondary via 15000/1, DT-??, tdef 3.00 s ?? PENDING-COORDINATION,
  USER_ASSERTED_PENDING_DOC, inverse prohibited — never dispatched to `phase5_time`).
- Coordination matrix v2 (96 rows, as found): **FAIL = 20, NO-TRIP = 28, NO-PAIR = 24,
  NOT DETERMINABLE FROM AVAILABLE DATA = 24, PASS = 0 (production-v2, 96 rows)**. Identical counts appear in
  `phase5_coordination_margins.csv`. No margin was tuned; shortfalls are study-setting coordination shortfalls
  reported honestly (see Sections 9 and 17).
- Breaker duty v2 (81 rows, as found): **40 x Q0 NOT DETERMINABLE FROM AVAILABLE DATA + 40 x 52G PASS +
  1 x Q0 NOTE**. That is 40 Q0 rows with no interrupting rating sourced, 40 52G rows PASS vs the sourced
  52G/GCB-10BAC10 100 kA sym breaking rating, plus one informational NOTE (F3 LLL 50.530885 kA +1.06% vs the
  estimated 50 kA station reference). Equipment withstand (GIS 50 kA) lives only in equipment columns, never as
  an interrupting rating.
- Effectiveness v2 (`phase5b_effectiveness.csv`, 48 rows = 40 backbone + 8 Siemens-baseline F1 duplicates, as
  found): **ASSERTABLE-DETECT = 24, NOT-DETERMINABLE = 24**. F1/F2 primaries assertable (87G/87T); F3/F4/F5
  primaries NOT-DETERMINABLE (87B/7SD settings missing; F5 out-of-zone). Primary timing 0.045 s derived
  fast-main clearing applies only to F1/87G + 52G identified; all other primary times NaN with reasons (see
  Section 16).
- Low-earth-fault physics preserved: F1 LG **7.272 A** primary -> **0.4848 mA** secondary through
  15000/1, covered by the 5 A sensitive EF study pickup with margin **1.454**; branch-through-current
  F1 LG GEN_Q **8.4141 kA** pinned by audit (never a bus total).
- Sensitivity (60 rows, all scope SENSITIVITY): 16000/1 recomputation fenced to generator-CT scope only.
  Validation **16/16** frozen-framework legs; suite **355 passed / 0 failed** at the v2 stamp (v1 suite 344/0 is
  frozen in the §20 v1 appendix).

## 2. Scope and freeze boundary (S1 reclassification)

In scope (v2): physical protection architecture (device presence rows, zones G/T/B/L, 52G breaker, CT cores),
CT conversion via sourced ratios, inverse-time library on study rows only, pickup methodology per master §21
rule (1.20x maximum load), operating-time calculation on study SI rows via frozen `phase5_time`,
coordination matrix + margins on backup-OC pairs, two-class TCC figures (physical DT vs study SI),
breaker-duty engine with rating split (interrupting vs equipment withstand), fenced sensitivity,
provenance ledger incl. USER_ASSERTED_PENDING_DOC, 16-leg frozen validation + B-legs, writer +
production-v2 driver, effectiveness table, this report, quality gate.

Out of scope (explicitly excluded): stability/AVR/SFC studies, relay vendor selection,
field-test procedures, equipment procurement ratings, any revision of Phase-3 or Phase-4 results. No claim is
made that every installed function was simulated; functions without sourced thresholds appear as presence rows
with MISSING settings.

Freeze boundary: `matlab/data/*`, `matlab/build/*`, `rev2/*`, `matlab/phase4/*`, `PHASE3_*`,
`results/phase4_fault/*`, and `results/phase5_protection/*` were read-only inputs. Phase-5b adds new
`phase5b_*` modules alongside frozen v1 files and writes the new tag production-v2 under
`results/phase5_protection_v2/`. The regression leg (R0) proves import identity before any output: F3 LLL OUT
= 50.5308851865359 kA (tolerance 1e-6) and F1 LG OUT = 0.00727200442799167 kA (tolerance 1e-9).

## 3. Input fault matrix (2 x 5 x 4 backbone)

`phase5_fault_inputs.csv` (40 rows) is the backbone import: stage `Ikpp`, `m = 0.5`, first row per
(caseID, location, fault_type) in backbone-first merge order — SOURCE-BACKED Phase-4 import
(`phase5_import`). F1 and F2 share one node but are kept as **distinct labelled rows with identical
values** (no artificial impedance invented); F4 primary rows carry `m = 0.5`. Fault types
LLL/LG/LL/LLG are all present for every (case, location) pair; the primary cases are
`LF360_GAT_OUT` (base) and `LF360_GAT_IN` (GAT-IN leg), never double-counted (manifest backbone:
80 solves = 40 Ikpp + 40 ip).

Representative backbone totals: F1 LLL OUT 126.21414119005 kA; F1 LG OUT 0.00727200442799167 kA
(7.272 A, NER-limited earth physics); F3 LLL OUT 50.5308851865359 kA; F4 LLL OUT 51.0575960885088 kA.

## 4. Device registry, topology and CT ledger (v2, 33 rows)

`phase5_device_registry.csv` (33 rows = 7 corrected study rows + 26 physical presence/control rows). Study rows
(layer STUDY) carry corrected CTs and TMS; physical rows (layer PHYSICAL) carry presence with settings only

Generator reference (physical reference only): 458 MVA / 22 kV / **12019 A** / PF 0.85; Imax **14309 A**
(SOURCE-BACKED nameplate datum). 360 MW is an operating point, never a nameplate. Legacy
16000/1 appears only with `ct_source = LEGACY` and is fenced to generator-CT sensitivity scope.

## 5. CT secondary conversion

`phase5_ct`: pure arithmetic `Isec_A = I_primary_A / ct_ratio`; the ledger fencing lives in
`ct_tag`/scope/provenance, never in the arithmetic. v2 CTs are 15000/1 (GEN, SOURCE-BACKED) and 1600/1
(GSUT/GIS, SOURCE-BACKED). Spot conversions:

- 12019 A -> 0.8012667 A secondary (via 15000/1).
- F1 LG 7.27200442799167 A -> **0.0004848 A (0.4848 mA)** secondary (sensitive-EF regime; the
  low-earth-fault physics survives CT conversion).
- F1 LLL GEN branch 55048.71 A -> 3.66991398 A secondary (via 15000/1); GSUT_HV branch 72105.15 A ->
  45.06572141 A secondary (via 1600/1).
- GEN-51-SI 17170.8 A -> 1.14472 A secondary; GEN-51-SIEMENS-BL 17171 A -> 1.1447 A secondary
  (cross-check 1.20x14309 = 17170.8 ≈ 17171, rel-err 0.000012); GSUT-HV-51 1380 A -> 0.8625 A;
  GIS-Q0-51 1043.94798235109 A -> 0.652467 A.

`phase5_relay_currents.csv` (108 rows) distinguishes phase-branch current (`I_primary_A`),
zero-sequence current (`I0_A` with `I0_source`) and secondary current (`I_secondary_A`) on every
row. Neutral impedance is counted exactly once: GEN-51N F1 LG relay current 7.27200443 A equals
3 x I0 (I0 = 0.00242400147600 kA), never 9 x I0. Branch currents are branch-through-current legs
(GEN_Q / GSUT_HV / GRID_Q / LINE B1/B2); bus totals never proxy relay current (the 43758.86 A-style totals
appear nowhere in detection logic).

## 6. Curve library (study constants + physical DT separation)

`phase5_curve` centralises the inverse-time formulation `t = TMS x k / ((I/Is)^alpha - 1)`
(`M = I/Is`; `M <= 1` -> `Inf`, i.e. no trip), plus definite-time/instantaneous routing
(`phase5_curve_dt`; default path has no `Iinst`, so nothing trips instantaneously by accident).
Study constants, single-sourced in `phase5_curve_info` and labelled STUDY: SI k = 0.14 / alpha = 0.02;
VI k = 13.5 / alpha = 1.0; EI k = 80 / alpha = 2.0. Production-v2 uses the SI family on study rows with

1: # Ashuganj 450 MW CCPP (South) - Final Master Data for AC/DC Studies
2: ## Context package for MATLAB/Simulink/Simscape Electrical, fault analysis and protection studies
3: 
4: **Purpose:** This document consolidates the current Ashuganj South CCPP data collected from the project technical documents, the newly obtained generator/transformer dataset, the current PGCB line-data PDF, the Siemens/TSK GIS as-built drawings, the PGCB/JICA grid study, and selected web references. It provides a single working dataset for the complete project.
5: 
6: ### Data-status legend
7: - **A - Project/official source:** directly stated in an uploaded project/PGCB/APSCL/Siemens document or official public record.
8: - **B - Strong secondary/project-supplied:** technically specific data from a supplied workbook or secondary study; use, but retain source/provenance note.
9: - **C - Engineering assumption:** missing plant-specific value filled with a realistic non-zero value for simulation. **Never describe C-values as measured plant facts.**
10: - **D - Derived:** calculated from sourced values using the equation shown.
11:

207: | Neutral | **Solidly grounded** | B |
208: | Excitation-related transformer data | As supplied | B |
209: 
210: ### Derived GSUT resistance/reactance
211: 
212: Taking the difference between full-load and no-load losses as load/copper loss:
213: 
214: \[
215: R_{pu} = \frac{0.9122}{515}=0.001771
216: \]
217: 
218: Then:
219: 
220: \[
221: X_{pu}=\sqrt{0.1663^2-0.001771^2}
222: \approx0.16629
223: \]
224: 
225: Therefore use, provisionally:
226: 
227: \[
228: \boxed{R_1=0.001771\ pu,\quad X_1\approx0.16629\ pu}
229: \]
230: 
231: on the 515-MVA transformer base.
232: 
233: For initial fault studies, use the same leakage magnitude for positive/negative sequence and explicitly apply the YNd1 zero-sequence blocking/grounding behavior in the sequence model.
234: 
235: **Note:** `0.00034%` no-load current from the supplied workbook is not trusted until the source sheet is re-checked.

512: # 11. LINE-ASSUMPTION BASIS
513: 
514: The assumptions are deliberately non-zero and are constrained by published examples.
515: 
516: - A 400-kV benchmark line has typical values near **R1 = 0.0209 ohm/km, X1 = 0.3192 ohm/km, B1 = 5.19 uS/km; R0 = 0.303 ohm/km, X0 = 1.189 ohm/km, B0 = 3.17 uS/km**. Our 400-kV Twin-Finch values are chosen close to this range while reflecting the actual high-capacity bundle. (OPAL-RT typical 400-kV benchmark.)
517: - A published 230-kV overhead-line example gives approximately **Z1 = 0.060 + j0.472 ohm/km** and **Z0 = 0.230 + j1.590 ohm/km**. (SEL technical paper.)
518: - Conductor references give approximately **0.0509 ohm/km at 20 C for Finch 1113 MCM** and approximately **0.0715-0.0719 ohm/km at 20 C for Mallard 795 MCM**. Published Grosbeak 636 data are around **0.0899 ohm/km at 20 C for ACSR**. These support the resistance scale used above.
519: 
520: **Engineering rule:** if a PGCB line-parameter report is later obtained, replace all C-values immediately and retain the current values only for preliminary/sensitivity analysis.

# 11. LINE-ASSUMPTION BASIS

The assumptions are deliberately non-zero and are constrained by published examples.

- A 400-kV benchmark line has typical values near **R1 = 0.0209 ohm/km, X1 = 0.3192 ohm/km, B1 = 5.19 uS/km; R0 = 0.303 ohm/km, X0 = 1.189 ohm/km, B0 = 3.17 uS/km**. Our 400-kV Twin-Finch values are chosen close to this range while reflecting the actual high-capacity bundle. (OPAL-RT typical 400-kV benchmark.)
- A published 230-kV overhead-line example gives approximately **Z1 = 0.060 + j0.472 ohm/km** and **Z0 = 0.230 + j1.590 ohm/km**. (SEL technical paper.)
- Conductor references give approximately **0.0509 ohm/km at 20 C for Finch 1113 MCM** and approximately **0.0715-0.0719 ohm/km at 20 C for Mallard 795 MCM**. Published Grosbeak 636 data are around **0.0899 ohm/km at 20 C for ACSR**. These support the resistance scale used above.

**Engineering rule:** if a PGCB line-parameter report is later obtained, replace all C-values immediately and retain the current values only for preliminary/sensitivity analysis.
